finding_short: Large flames grow until radiative heat loss extinguishes them; flame size rises with reactant flow and falls with ambient oxygen.
quote: Large flames increase in size over time until the flame extinguishes due to radiative heat loss.
source_title: Laminar Non-Premixed Flames of Gaseous Fuel Aboard the International Space Station

finding_short: Flame size increases as reactant flow rate rises and as ambient oxygen falls.
quote: Flame size increases with reactant flow rate and decreases with ambient oxygen concentration.
source_title: Laminar Non-Premixed Flames of Gaseous Fuel Aboard the International Space Station

finding_short: Supplying nitrogen with the fuel suppressed soot entirely in ethylene spherical flames in drop-tower tests.
quote: In these flames, structure has a defining influence on soot production, with soot suppressed entirely when nitrogen is supplied with the fuel.
source_title: Flame Design: A Novel Approach Developed to Produce Clean, Efficient Diffusion Flames

finding_short: In ISS tests, still-air microgravity flames self-extinguished below about 25 percent oxygen, but burned for minutes above it.
quote: While the flames can burn for minutes in elevated oxygen concentrations, like those being considered for future spacecraft, they were found to self-extinguish in concentrations below ~25% (by volume).
source_title: Laminar Non-Premixed Flames of Gaseous Fuel Aboard the International Space Station

finding_short: Larger flames generally self-extinguished within 1.5 minutes, while smaller flames burned for minutes at elevated oxygen.
quote: While smaller flames can burn for minutes at elevated oxygen concentrations, larger flames were generally seen to self-extinguish within 1.5 minutes.
source_title: Laminar Non-Premixed Flames of Gaseous Fuel Aboard the International Space Station

finding_short: Low-momentum microgravity flames can burn for minutes with no air flow or flame spread.
quote: Low-momentum microgravity flames can burn for minutes in the absence of an air flow or flame spread.
source_title: Laminar Non-Premixed Flames of Gaseous Fuel Aboard the International Space Station

finding_short: Sooty microgravity coflow flames were taller, wider and held 5x to 8x more soot than 1-g flames.
quote: Sooty microgravity flames are taller & wider and contain 5x to 8x more soot than equivalent 1G flames.
source_title: Laminar Non-Premixed Flames of Gaseous Fuel Aboard the International Space Station

finding_short: Microgravity widened the fuel-dilution limits; near limits, flames were more stable and could lift off at lower fuel concentration.
quote: Microgravity increases the limits of fuel dilution.
source_title: Laminar Non-Premixed Flames of Gaseous Fuel Aboard the International Space Station

finding_short: Flame luminosity, combustion intensity and ion current were clearly correlated.
quote: There are clear correlations between flame luminosity, combustion intensity, and ion current.
source_title: Laminar Non-Premixed Flames of Gaseous Fuel Aboard the International Space Station

finding_short: Highly diluted flames could be stabilized with very weak electric fields.
quote: Highly-diluted flames can be stabilized with very weak electric fields.
source_title: Laminar Non-Premixed Flames of Gaseous Fuel Aboard the International Space Station

finding_short: Radiative extinction appeared at high flow rates and kinetic extinction at low flow rates.
quote: Radiative extinction seems to occur at high flow rates and kinetic extinction at low flow rates.
source_title: Laminar Non-Premixed Flames of Gaseous Fuel Aboard the International Space Station

finding_short: Helium instead of nitrogen dilution shifted extinction limits and made kinetic extinction hard to discern.
quote: With helium, rather than nitrogen, dilution of both the fuel and oxygen, the extinction limits are shifted and kinetic extinction is generally difficult to discern.
source_title: Laminar Non-Premixed Flames of Gaseous Fuel Aboard the International Space Station

finding_short: PMMA rods spread steadily at 13.6 percent oxygen in microgravity, below the 16 percent 1-g blowoff limit.
quote: The 1g blowoff for the ¼” rod is at 16% oxygen, whereas we obtained steady spreading at 13.6% oxygen in BASS-II.
source_title: Combustion of Solids in Microgravity: Results from the BASS-II Experiment
source_note: BASS-II ISS microgravity result for 1/4 inch PMMA rod versus 1-g limit

finding_short: Normal-gravity flammability limits should be de-rated by at least the 2.4 percent negative oxygen margin of safety.
quote: Thus the material has a negative Oxygen Margin of Safety of 2.4% O2, and the normal gravity flammability limits should be de-rated by at least that much.
source_title: Combustion of Solids in Microgravity: Results from the BASS-II Experiment

finding_short: A BASS-II-scale fire diluted in the US Lab would give about 1.5 ppm CO, below the 10 ppm limit.
quote: the combustion products from a fire of the scale of a BASS–II test would quickly be diluted, so that even within just the U.S. Lab (106-m3 pressurized volume), the CO levels in the lab would only be 1.5 ppm, well below spacecraft maximum allowable concentration (SMAC) values for even long-term exposure (10 ppm), let alone the 1 hour SMAC of 55 ppm (Ref. 12).
source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report
habitat_note: US Lab, 106 cubic metre pressurized volume

finding_short: A tiny acrylic flame burned over 5 minutes before self-extinguishing, so it might go undetected for a long time.
quote: even these burned for over 5 minutes before self-extinguishing. This has implications for spacecraft fire safety since a tiny flame might be undetected for a long time.
source_title: Thickness and Fuel Preheating Effects on Material Flammability in Microgravity from the BASS Experiment

finding_short: At speeds under 1 cm/s the flames became dim blue and very stable.
quote: At the lowest speeds examined (less than 1 cms) all the flames tended to become dim blue and very stable.
source_title: Thickness and Fuel Preheating Effects on Material Flammability in Microgravity from the BASS Experiment

finding_short: Large n-alkane droplets kept burning at low temperature after the visible flame went out; small droplets burned out or extinguished.
quote: Large n-alkane droplets exhibited quasi-steady low-temperature burning and extinction following radiative extinction of the visible flame while smaller droplets burned to completion or disruptively extinguished.
source_title: Cool-flame Extinction During N-Alkane Droplet Combustion in Microgravity

finding_short: Background particle levels in the ISS cabin were far below shuttle and ground levels.
quote: The ISS cabin was found to be a very clean environment with particulate levels substantially below the space shuttle and typical ground-based environments.
source_title: Particle and Smoke Detection on ISS for Next Generation Smoke Detectors

finding_short: PMMA rod flames ignited at higher oxygen survived down to 13.6 percent O2.
quote: Despite this limiting O2 concentration for ignition, flames ignited at a higher O2 survived to final O2 concentrations as low as 13.6 percent O2, indicating that the high heat loss to the initially cold rod will quench a postignition flame while a developed solid phase temperature profile allows a sustained flame down to these low ambient O2 concentrations.
source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report
source_note: Section 6.1 of the BASS-II Summary Report has the same title as the publication listed on the PSI-62 record

finding_short: ISS droplet tests showed large n-alkane droplets burning quasi-steadily at low temperature after radiative extinction.
quote: large n-alkane droplets can continue to burn quasi-steadily following radiative extinction in a low-temperature regime
source_title: Cool-flame Extinction During N-Alkane Droplet Combustion in Microgravity

finding_short: Limiting oxygen index for methanol droplets in these diluent gases was about 12 to 13 percent oxygen by volume.
quote: The experiments also show that the limiting oxygen index for methanol in these diluent gases is around 12% to 13% oxygen by volume.
source_title: Methanol Droplet Combustion in Oxygen-Inert Environments in Microgravity

finding_short: At one atmosphere, methanol droplets ignited and burned somewhat at 13 percent oxygen in nitrogen.
quote: At one atmosphere pressure, ignition and some burning were observed for an oxygen concentration of 13% with the rest being nitrogen.
source_title: Methanol Droplet Extinction in Oxygen/Carbon-dioxide/Nitrogen Mixtures in Microgravity: Results from the International Space Station Experiments

finding_short: Observed limiting oxygen index values for the two fuels were slightly lower than initially expected.
quote: Observed LOI values for these fuels appear to be slightly lower than initially expected.
source_title: Detailed Results from the Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) March 2009 to December 2011

finding_short: Saffire-I burned a 94 cm by 40.6 cm fabric at 20 cm/s: 1.8 mm/s spread, about 1200 W flame power.
quote: Average flame spread rate is 1.8 mm/s; estimated average flame power is 1200 +/- 300 W
source_title: Saffire: A Novel Approach to Study of Spacecraft Fire Safety Using Un-Manned Spacecraft
habitat_note: Cygnus unmanned spacecraft, unberthed from ISS

finding_short: Large thin-fabric flames spread steadily in low gravity, unlike in normal gravity.
quote: Flame spread over a large thin charring surface in low-gravity showed that steady flame spread was possible (unlike normal gravity).
source_title: Saffire: A Novel Approach to Study of Spacecraft Fire Safety Using Un-Manned Spacecraft

finding_short: In the concurrent test, flame size stayed constrained after ignition, unlike an upward flame in 1-g.
quote: For the concurrent flame spread test, the flame size remained constrained after the ignition transient, which is not the case in 1-g.
source_title: Results of Large-Scale Spacecraft Flammability Tests
source_note: Abstract describes the 94 x 40.6 cm fabric test, the Saffire-I sample size

finding_short: Concurrent spread was more sensitive to flow duct size than previously expected.
quote: Concurrent flame spread (with the wind) was shown to be more sensitive to the flow duct dimension than previously anticipated.
source_title: Saffire: A Novel Approach to Study of Spacecraft Fire Safety Using Un-Manned Spacecraft

finding_short: Saffire-II sample 2-1 gave an insignificant burn in microgravity but burned completely in normal gravity.
quote: 2-1 80 W 9.2 s Insignificant ~ 0 n/a ~ Complete Acceleratory
source_title: Saffire: A Novel Approach to Study of Spacecraft Fire Safety Using Un-Manned Spacecraft
source_note: Row of the Saffire-I-III results table; sample ids follow the table in the same document

finding_short: Saffire-I and -III: flame spread speed scaled with the air flow (20 vs 25 cm/s).
quote: The flame speed is proportional to the air flow velocity
source_title: Saffire: A Novel Approach to Study of Spacecraft Fire Safety Using Un-Manned Spacecraft
source_note: Row of the Saffire-I-III results table

finding_short: Saffire-III fabric burn at higher flow: 2.3 mm/s spread, about 84 cm burn length in microgravity.
quote: 3-1 182 W 8 s 300 s ~ 84 cm 2.3 mm/s Complete Acceleratory
source_title: Saffire: A Novel Approach to Study of Spacecraft Fire Safety Using Un-Manned Spacecraft
source_note: Row of the Saffire-I-III results table

finding_short: Most average smoke particle sizes in the reflight were 200 to 400 nm; quiescent cases sometimes gave much larger particles.
quote: Overall the majority of the average smoke particle sizes were found to be in the 200 nm to 400 nm range with the quiescent cases producing some cases with substantially larger particles.
source_title: Particle Morphology and Size Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-2
source_note: Abstract names the Reflight (SAME-2), the experiment recorded as SAME-R

finding_short: Test materials emitted most of their particulate in the submicron range.
quote: For the conditions tested, the materials emit most of their particulate in the submicron range.
source_title: Particle Morphology Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight

finding_short: The ISS detector gave a weak signal for some Teflon runs because of particle size.
quote: The ISS detector showed a relatively weak signal for some Teflon runs doubtless a result of the particle size.
source_title: Particle Morphology Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight

finding_short: Zero air flow produced smoke particles 2 to 3 times larger than 8 cm/s flow.
quote: The zero flow conditions produced smoke particles that were 2 to 3 times larger than those produced at the nominal 8 cm/s flow rate.
source_title: Particle Morphology and Size Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-2

finding_short: All samples made many sub-micron particles that an ionization detector reads easily.
quote: all samples produced significant numbers of sub-micron particulate that are readily detected using an ionization smoke detector.
source_title: Particle Morphology and Size Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-2

finding_short: Microgravity sooting flames had lower soot temperatures and higher soot volume fraction than normal-gravity flames.
quote: The microgravity sooting flames were found to have lower soot temperatures and higher volume fraction than their normal gravity counterparts.
source_title: An Experimental and Computational Study on Soot Formation in a Coflow Jet Flame Under Microgravity and Normal Gravity

finding_short: Microgravity coflow flames were noticeably longer than their 1-g counterparts.
quote: computed and measured nonbuoyant flames are noticeably longer than their 1g counterparts;
source_title: A Computational and Experimental Study of Coflow Laminar Methane/Air Diffusion Flames: Effects of Fuel Dilution, Inlet Velocity, and Gravity
